decisions.reason: Although its later visibility is unclear, the reusable citrus harvesting crate remains close to the firm's core crate engineering and reusable-packaging know-how, so management would more likely refine or reposition it than withdraw it outright.

The foldable large container is strongly aligned with the firm's established container platform and multi-model engineering capabilities, giving it high learning value and a good chance of continued retention.

A stackable plastic crate fits the firm's central product and process knowledge very well, so even with uncertain market visibility the firm would usually keep it while absorbing customer feedback and optimizing the range.
This medium-duty rackable pallet builds directly on the firm's pallet and logistics expertise, making continued improvement and selective commercialization more likely than exit within a year.

The plastic pallet with load retainers is still related to the firm's core pallet knowledge, but as a more specialized variant it faces somewhat higher rationalization risk if demand does not justify ongoing portfolio complexity.
